title: The Sigil of Highmoor
premise: Dominic Dravenmoor, an exiled storm-caller hiding her gift behind a guild clerk's ink-stained hands, discovers the ledgers she keeps record shipments of captured magic-bearers sold to the crown. When the royal hunt reaches Highmoor, she must choose between the guild master who once sheltered her and the smuggler boy who knows what she is. Uncovering that the hunt is a cover for harvesting sigils to awaken a dormant war-construct beneath the capital, Dominic rallies the hunted to break the guild's complicity. In the end she publicly claims her stolen name and her storm, shattering the construct and the guild's silence alike, though exile becomes her permanent country.
about_author: Zephyrine Vasquez is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloging smugglers' manifests before turning to fiction. She writes storm-soaked fantasy about people whose loyalties cost more than their lives.

chapters.title: Ink and Iron Rain
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. She catalogs an impossible cargo — a caged moth made of moonlight — while suppressing a storm rising in her chest. A clerk's slip nearly exposes her gift. Emotional beat: the suffocating discipline of a life spent hiding in plain sight.

chapters.title: The Crown's Proclamation
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Royal criers announce the hunt for the gifted; guild master Corvane orders all 'irregular stock' moved before inspectors arrive. Dominic recognizes a ledger entry bearing her own erased family sigil. Emotional beat: dread curdling into resolve.

chapters.title: A Boy Who Reads Backwards
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. A young smuggler who can read mirrored script decodes a ledger page and finds the guild sells captives, not contraband. He confronts Dominic, guessing her secret from the way she steadies his shaking hands. Emotional beat: wary alliance born of mutual blackmail.

chapters.title: The Vault Beneath Highmoor
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Following the ledgers, they find a vault of harvested sigils — crystallized magic pried from the hunted. Dominic touches one and her storm answers, nearly betraying them. Emotional beat: grief and horror at what her silence has funded.

chapters.title: What Corvane Owes
chapters.summary: Corvane's POV. Flashback and present: he sheltered Dominic after her family's execution, but the crown holds his debt over him. He betrays Wren to the hunters to buy time. Emotional beat: a protector rationalizing his first unforgivable act.

chapters.title: Chains on the King's Road
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren, caged in a convict caravan, organizes the captured gifted using coded knocks. Dominic shadows the convoy, torn between fleeing with the ledgers and attacking alone. Emotional beat: loyalty stretched to its breaking point.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Names
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. She discovers the final ledger: the sigils feed a war-construct buried beneath the capital, and the hunt's end date is coronation day. She must decide whether to burn the ledgers — erasing the victims' names — or use them as a map. Emotional beat: the cost of truth versus mercy.

chapters.title: Storm over the Assizes
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. At the public assizes where the captured are sentenced, Dominic calls the storm she has buried for ten years, breaking the cages open as Wren frees the prisoners from within. Emotional beat: catharsis — identity claimed at last, at the price of anonymity forever.

chapters.title: The Construct Wakes
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. The coronation ritual, half-fed by escaped sigils, raises the construct anyway; Dominic realizes destroying it means feeding it her own storm. Corvane arrives, choosing at last to stand between her and the hunters. Emotional beat: sacrifice reframed — not erasure, but authorship.

chapters.title: The Sigil of Highmoor
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. She pours her storm into the construct and unmakes it, surviving as an ordinary-seeming woman whose gift is spent. The guild falls; the hunted scatter with the ledger of names read aloud in the square. Wren stays; Dominic walks the open road, finally unhidden. Emotional beat: quiet, hard-won peace.
